note: Newest first. 'at' is an ISO timestamp; omit the time and it shows just the date. 'by' is who asked for it.

releases.title: Likeness ratio, ranked
items: The list is ordered by how much each person actually counts, strongest first, with anyone you've nothing in common with at the bottom.
Ranked by influence rather than the raw percentage — one shared title always reads 100%, and that shouldn't sit above someone with thirty.

releases.title: Whose list you're looking at
items: Watch lists and suggestions are personal — the who dropdown only governs the shared archive. That wasn't stated anywhere, so pointing the dropdown at someone else looked like a bug.
Both tabs now say so when the dropdown is set to another member, and the guide explains it.

releases.title: Trailers that won't play in the US
items: TMDB often lists a foreign-territory upload first, and those are blocked here — the player can't detect it, so you just got 'Video unavailable'.
US and English uploads are now preferred, official trailers before teasers.
A bar under the player names the video and offers 'Won't play — try another', plus links to open it on YouTube or search.

releases.title: The ledger opens on your own titles
items: With several members, defaulting to Everyone made it unclear whose ratings you were reading. It now opens on yours, and Everyone is still one click away.
Whichever you pick is remembered for next time.

releases.title: Add someone else's title to your own ledger
items: Opening an entry logged by another member now offers Want to see and 'I've seen it — log it'. Before there was only the trailer button, so there was no way to act on what you were reading.
Neither appears if it's already in your ledger.

releases.title: Click a recommended title to do something with it
items: Clicking a title in 'Recommend to each other' opens a panel with the poster, who else has rated it and how, and buttons to watch the trailer, add it to your watch list, or log it.
It used to jump to the Ledger and search for a title you hadn't logged, which found nothing.

releases.title: Act on a recommendation where you see it
items: Titles someone would pass to you now have Want to see and I've seen it, so you can queue or log them without going to Log a Film.
The entries query pages through everything rather than stopping at Supabase's 1000-row limit — precautionary, but it would have bitten as the household grows.

releases.title: The ledger was being truncated
items: Supabase returns at most 1000 rows for a plain query. With seven members that ceiling was being passed, so part of the archive silently went missing — which is why recommendations offered titles you'd already watched.
The query now pages through everything.
The recommend controls stack properly on a phone instead of squashing into a column.

releases.title: Taste match only shows what it can measure
items: With seven members there are 21 pairings, and listing the empty ones buried anything real. Now only pairs with something in common appear, best match first.
Pairs one or two titles short of comparable show how many more are needed; the rest are summarised in a single line.

releases.title: Tell me what you think of a change
items: Once you're past the how-to guide, signing in shows anything that's changed since you were last here.
Each change has a yes / not really. Choosing 'not really' opens a box to say what's wrong with it.
Feedback is saved to the archive and, if a webhook is configured, emailed to Chris.

releases.title: Guide lives in its own file
items: The how-to popup now reads from guide.json instead of being baked into the page, so it can be updated without touching code.
It carries a version. Bump it after a change and everyone sees the guide once more, so they pick up what's new — then it goes quiet again.
Still three showings for a new member, and the Guide button any time.

releases.title: Guide shows three times
items: New members get the how-to popup on their first three sign-ins rather than once, then it stops.
The count lives on their profile, so it follows them between phone and laptop instead of restarting on each device.
It says how many more times they'll see it, and the Guide button always brings it back.

releases.title: Recommendations one pair at a time
items: 'Recommend to each other' was every pairing at once. Now you pick one person and see a single direction.
Defaults to what they'd pass to you; Swap direction flips it to what you'd pass to them.
Sorted by their rating, loved first, and each title clicks through to its dossier.

releases.title: Likeness ratio
items: Suggestions now take account of what the rest of the household thinks, weighted by how closely each person's ratings track yours — the likeness ratio.
It grows with the number of titles you've both rated, so three in common counts a little and thirty counts a lot. Someone who consistently disagrees with you pulls a title down instead of up.
Capped at 0.85x to 1.15x — deliberately the gentlest lever in the engine. Your own ratings still decide.
Cards say who: 'Chase loved it · Damon rated it 4★'.
The Household tab shows each person's current ratio and what it's based on.

releases.title: A guide for new members
items: First time someone signs in with an empty ledger, a short guide explains what each tab does.
A Guide button next to Sign out reopens it any time.

releases.title: Everyone gets their own ledger
items: A member with no profile row was having their own entries hidden from them — their own rows now always show.
Falls back to the account name instead of 'Someone' until a profile exists.
Comes with SQL that removes any leftover uniqueness rule stopping two people logging the same title, and backfills missing profiles.

releases.title: Change a rating from the dossier
items: Open any of your entries and there's a star selector next to How you felt — change it there instead of deleting and re-logging.
Re-rating rebuilds your suggestions, since ratings are what the engine seeds from.

releases.title: Watch list knows what you've watched
items: Anything on the watch list that's already in your ledger is marked WATCHED, dimmed, and offers a link to the entry instead of 'I've seen it'.
A banner at the top counts them and clears them all in one click.
Logging a title already removes it from the list; this catches anything that slipped through before that existed.

releases.title: No double logging
items: Search results now show WATCHED on anything already in your ledger, instead of a match score — search only ever checked the filmography view before.
Clicking a watched result won't open the rating form; it offers to take you to the entry in the ledger instead.
The save button refuses a duplicate as a last line of defence, so it can't happen by any route.
The Want to see button is hidden on titles you've already watched.
Trailer buttons on search results and filmography cards — the poster there is the select-to-log target, so there was nowhere to click for a trailer.
A title already in your ledger now looks it — the card dims, the name gets a tick, and the button reads 'In your ledger'. Clicking gives it a nudge rather than silently doing nothing.

releases.title: Not interested, on the Patterns strip too
items: The discovery strip under a Patterns chart now has a Not interested button, like What's Next.
It also respects things you've already dismissed — it was ignoring them and offering the same titles back.

releases.title: Match scores on search results
items: Search results and filmography pages now show a match percentage, so you can tell whether something is your kind of thing before logging it.
It's worked out backwards from the suggestions engine: TMDB is asked what a title sits near, and that's measured against your ledger, then weighted by genre and by directors and cast you rate highly.
Scores are cached until your ledger changes, so repeat searches are instant.
People chips in search results are readable on the dark palettes — the buttons weren't inheriting a text colour.
Small print — role labels, credit counts, entry times, secondary buttons — now clears AAA contrast on all eight palettes instead of leaning on the muted grey.

releases.title: Search results ranked by what's usable
items: TMDB sorts search by text relevance, so obscure titles with no poster and no year were outranking the ones you'd actually want. Results now lead with artwork, then how well known the title is.
The blank placeholder for a missing poster is shorter, so a few data-less results no longer fill the screen.

releases.title: Crew Index counts, readable
items: Back to a single number beside each name.
Each title now carries its own credit count — Ben Berman reads 5 with 'The Amazing Johnathan Documentary ×5', so the total visibly adds up.
Titles within a row sort by how much work the person did on them.

releases.title: Add to watch list from search
items: Search results and filmography pages now have a Want to see button, so you can queue something without logging it as watched.
Anything already flagged shows On your list instead.

releases.title: Crew Index counts
items: The number beside each name counts credits, not titles — someone who shot, edited and directed one film showed as 3.
It now reads credits / titles when they differ, and Repeat collaborators means more than one title rather than more than one job.

releases.title: Coming soon
items: Unreleased titles get a diagonal COMING SOON band across the poster, a pill in the ledger, and an expected date in the dossier.
Release dates were being fetched and thrown away; they're kept now, with a one-time backfill for older entries.
Films years out often have no date at all, so TMDB's production status is what flags them.

releases.title: Household membership
items: The household now has an owner — whoever signed up first — and only the owner can remove someone.
Removing a member blocks their access and stops their entries counting, but deletes nothing. You can let them back in.
Enforced in the database rather than by hiding a button, so it holds even against someone calling the API directly.
Ownership itself can't be reassigned by anyone but the owner.
Titles in the Crew Index are clickable too — click one to open its dossier in the ledger.

releases.title: Search people, not just titles
items: Log a Film now finds actors and directors as well as films and series — the people were always in the results, they were just being thrown away.
Click a person to see up to 24 of their titles, directing credits first, with anything already in your ledger marked LOGGED.
Every credited name in a dossier and in the Crew Index is now clickable through to that person's filmography.

releases.title: Directors and cast now count
items: Match scores now weigh who made a title, not just what people co-watch with it. Directors count most, then writers, then top-billed cast.
A director you keep rating highly — Skye Borgman, say — now lifts their other work up the list.
Cards say who: "Skye Borgman directed one you rated."
Credits are cached in your browser, so the first rebuild costs about a second and a half and later ones are nearly free.

releases.title: Watch List ranks itself
items: Every Watch List card now shows a match score, and the grid sorts best-match-first by default.
The engine keeps a score for every candidate it considered, not just the visible 60, so titles flagged weeks ago still get a real number.
Titles never offered as candidates show a dash and sort last, rather than being treated as a zero.
Scores rebuild automatically when they're missing, instead of waiting for the next time you log something.

releases.title: Liked it, and loved it
items: The yes/no on Log a Film became three: Not for me, Liked it, Loved it.
A loved title pulls about 60% harder as a recommendation seed than a plain rating — real signal inside the five-star band.
Hollow heart for liked, solid for loved, and the masthead counts them separately.
Each dossier gained a 'How you felt' row, so you can promote older entries without deleting and re-logging them.

releases.title: Recent updates panel
items: The banner reads Recent updates and opens a panel with two tabs.
Archive: who added what, grouped by day, with a filter for each family member.
Site changes: this list.
Five more palettes — Noir, Drive-In, Technicolor, Nitrate, Terminal — and your palette and density now stick between visits.

releases.title: Personal ranking
items: My ranking sort on the Ledger: drag your own entries into the order you actually liked them, or use the arrows on a phone.
Ranks are fractional, so moving one title writes one row instead of renumbering the whole ledger.
Where you place a title feeds the suggestions — your number one pulls twice as hard as your last.

releases.title: Suggestions rebuilt from scratch
items: What's Next now rebuilds from your ledger every time you log something, instead of serving a list frozen in a file.

Scoring rebalanced three ways: a five-star favourite outweighs a three-star shrug by roughly 17x instead of 2x, genre affinity is back, and dense clusters of cross-referencing documentaries no longer bury titles only a couple of favourites point at.
New "Not interested" button, with undo and a reset.
Flagged titles leave What's Next and live on the Watch List instead.
Fixed: candidates were excluding anything anyone in the house had watched, which made "New to me" impossible to satisfy.
Service filter dropdown now fills in — it only ever offered "Any service".

releases.title: Watch List, and logging fixes
items: New Watch List tab — the titles you flagged had been saving all along with nowhere to show them.
Log a Film clears itself after saving. It used to keep the last rating, date, note and liked flag.
Watch date defaults to today from the local clock; anything logged after 7pm was being stamped with tomorrow's date.
Logging something clears it off the Watch List automatically.
Match badges are visible again — the trailer button had been painting over them since it went in.
